source_text: So, reviewing the examples: a multi-part work order should be accepted if all the parts are delivered; the agent should not sit there waiting after the first part is done (I mentioned this example already).  The next example is more complicated: if the task involves routing handoffs to some other agent(s) then the task is not done until those assignments have been made.  In fact, a task may involve many such assignments, bellbacks, handoffs, routing.  So the "handoff to another agent" is just a step in the chain.  But pausing there is not good.  Livee case: codex-18, line 6077.   NB. This probably needs a code-level intervention, not just strong words in the system prompt (which is long enough as it is).  We have a pattern called structure/cook-ting.flexiarg which is about understanding the "joints" of a problem, and a tee-shaped handoff situation is an example of such a "joint".  It's a bit like we're creating a "marble run" for the xiaoxiang marks, if that makes sense?  The fact that codex-18 is not using these marks makes it all the more difficult, but maybe their session predated the AGENTS.md change

reply_text:
㊥ (the two examples) Both examples are now in `E-agency-work-orders.md` as requirements:
- A multi-part order stays open until every part is delivered, and the agent keeps going instead of waiting after the first part.
- A handoff creates a child order under the parent. When an agent's job ends with its order open and a child order still open, Agency parks the agent on the child and resumes it when the child closes.

That parking is done in code, not by instructions in the system prompt. Committed as `a36401e0`, not pushed.

㊢ (the codex-18 case) Around line 6077 of codex-18's REPL buffer, codex-18 belled codex-19 asking it to *check* whether its latest revision supports `inspect`. codex-19 answered at 23:38: "This is my transpiler/runtime blocker … No fix revision exists yet." The reply reached codex-18 as an auto-bellback. codex-18 wrote that `atEnd` validation was "blocked awaiting that fix" and ended its turn. It isn't parked, and no order asks codex-19 for the fix.
- Every job in that chain is `done`, but the work isn't.
- The bell asked for a check where the work needed a fix.
- codex-19's "this is mine" commits it to the fix, but nothing records that as a promise.
- codex-18 stopped at the handoff (the tee) instead of waiting on the branch it opened.

🈯 (the marks) codex-18 does use the marks: its paragraphs in that stretch carry ㊥, ㊢, ㊬ and ㊟, and so does codex-19's reply. So its session isn't older than the AGENTS.md change. What was missing is code that keeps the work moving at the handoff, not the marks themselves.

🈖 (the marble run) The excursion adds your image. The marks are the marbles, and P24's adjacency table is the track, for example `:delegate → :promise → :fulfil`. A handoff is a tee in the track, the kind of joint the cook-ting pattern is about. The run has to send the marble down the branch and know where the branches rejoin. The codex-18 case is the marble coming to rest at the tee.

🈸 (the open fix) The `inspect` fix is still an order nobody has given. Shall I bell codex-19 to make the fix, and park codex-18 on it so the retest runs when it lands? codex-18 is your seat, so I won't touch it without your word. codex-19 is busy with another job at the moment.

(contents) The excursion has:
- **Requirements:** an order is a recorded act; a job ending doesn't close it; one reminder at turn end, then a problem report to the agent that asked; the kernel is the only judge; a listing route plus a count in the lighter.
- **What already exists:** parking, promises and the obligations projection, all of which serve only the agent that asked.
- **The P24 gap:** delivered work isn't recorded as closing the obligation.
